title: Integration health check - 2026-01-19
content:
Attendees: Aisha (owner), Miguel, Claire, Noah, Priya, Jordan

Agenda:
- Quick health summary for top active integrations
- Blockers / escalations for SLOs and capacity
- Risk matrix and proposed mitigations (canaries, fallbacks)
- Open actions and owners for next week

High-level summary:
- Overall integrations holding at expected throughput. Three customers show intermittent latency spikes during peak windows (details below). No production outages.
- Two active rollouts (Acadia and Borealis) are in canary stage; early telemetry shows token cost within 8% of forecast.
- KV-cache warmup inconsistency observed for quantized-7b fallback path; engineering to patch runtime logic (PR linked).

Per-customer notes:
1) Acadia (Fintech) — canary 15% traffic
- Progress: Canary started 2026-01-12, CPU/GPU utilization within expected. Slightly elevated p95 latency on short prompt patterns (<= 64 tokens).
- Blocker: intermittent prefix-cache misses leading to repeated KV-loads; appears correlated with request routing to a new dedicated pool after autoscale event.
- Impact: latency spikes ~200ms p95, customer acceptance test still green but margin thin for peak loads.
- Action: Miguel to attach runtime logs and trace for a missed prefix sequence (SEINT-4821). Engineering to roll small patch to cache TTL semantics by 2026-01-22.

2) Borealis (SaaS search) — canary 30% traffic, A/B rollout
- Progress: Re-ranking integration tests passed; embedding sync has 0.3% mismatch in vector dims vs expected (data mapping issue).
- Blocker: ingestion pipeline schema drift from their upstream; ProServices working with their data team to normalize.
- Impact: minor quality regressions on long tail queries. No perf regressions.
- Action: Claire to coordinate a one-hour edge case session with Borealis data team (tentative 2026-01-21). Patch for embedding coercion scheduled 2026-01-25 (JIRA SEINT-4877).

3) Meridian (Enterprise private deployment) — onboarding in dedicated mode
- Progress: Private control plane installed, KMS integration in-progress.
- Blockers: HSM key rotation policy conflicts with our current installer script; requires ops runbook update.
- Impact: deployment delay of ~3 business days if runbook not adjusted.
- Action: Noah + Jordan to produce runbook diff and a short demo recording by 2026-01-23.

4) TidalHealth (regulated) — pilot live, low traffic
- Progress: All audit logs flowing to customer S3. Privacy review flagged a minor metadata exposure in trace IDs.
- Blocker: trace id contains truncated email hash in certain debug modes. Needs redaction option.
- Action: Priya to open a security ticket and propose a config flag for redaction by 2026-01-24.

Operational notes / telemetry:
- Cost: Early canary telemetry aligns with forecast. Acadia slightly over budget on token churn due to cache misses. Recommend temporary increase to batching window to reduce per-token overhead while cache fix is deployed.
- Capacity: Dedicated pool headroom at 18% during peak; autoscaler behaved nominally but took ~45s to spin up extra nodes in one zone (investigate scaling timeliness).
- Observability: Tracing sample rates differ between hosted and dedicated environments; reconcile sample config to ensure comparable signals for canary analysis.

Risks & mitigation:
- Risk: If prefix-cache regression persists, customer P95 could exceed SLO for short prompts and trigger rollback.
  Mitigation: Hotfix cache TTL and enable fallback to quantized-7b variant with warmed KV on detection.
- Risk: Schema drift for embeddings can create silent quality regressions during rollouts.
  Mitigation: Add a lightweight embedding validator to the ingest path and gate rollout if mismatch rate > 0.2%.

Open action items (owners & due dates):
1) Miguel — attach full runtime traces for Acadia prefix-cache misses; due 2026-01-21.
2) Engineering (oncall/runtime) — implement cache TTL patch and deploy canary hotfix; due 2026-01-22.
3) Claire — schedule Borealis edge-case session and produce data mapping notes; due 2026-01-21.
4) Noah & Jordan — runbook diff + demo for Meridian private installer; due 2026-01-23.
5) Priya — security ticket and redaction flag proposal for TidalHealth; due 2026-01-24.
6) Observability team — align trace sampling across environments; create short runbook for comparing p95 across hosted/dedicated; due 2026-01-26.

Decisions made:
- Proceed with Acadia canary and apply cache TTL hotfix rather than immediate rollback.
- Increase canary traffic to Borealis to 40% after embedding coercion patch verifies quality thresholds in a staging run.

Parking lot / unresolved items:
- Need a lightweight metric for cache-warmth per model variant (how many requests hit warm KV vs cold). Ideas: augment telemetry with a boolean 'kv_warm' tag.
- Proposal to add a short brownout simulation to test fallback logic for quantized models during peak. Schedule next sprint discussion.

Notes to execs (one-liner):
- Integrations stable; targeted runtime cache fix + small data-mapping work will clear current quality and latency issues. No customer escalations requiring exec intervention today.

Next sync: 2026-01-26, 09:00 PST.

Quick checklist before next meeting:
- Confirm hotfix deploy timeline + smoke test plan (Miguel, eng runtime)
- Verify Borealis embedding patch in staging and sample quality checks (Claire)
- Share Meridian runbook diff with infra security (Noah/Jordan)
- Security signoff or mitigation plan for TidalHealth trace metadata (Priya)

Notes to self / freeform:
- Consider adding a small synthetic load that targets short prompts to catch cache miss patterns earlier.
- Follow up on autoscaler cold-start time in zone us-west-2; might be a provider-side constraint or scaling policy tuning.
